title: The Sleeping Animal
text:
You will suffer. You have suffered already.
Perhaps you are suffering now.
And though you know
why (if indeed you know),
that knowledge will not console you.

The farewell to your own; chance,
relentless; the mystery of the sky,
everything lost, facts and life below, time below,
or life above too, toward what awaits you,
everything shapes the taste of your tears,
a tasteless taste, since it is not shared
by the one who has seen you suffer
—cannot share it—,
a taste you do not understand,
a heap of tears that trace,
I do not know where, a sea
on which they sail, and I do not know why,
useless forever, inconsolable,
who knows since when,
their soul,
your soul
and mine.
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The poem’s repeated, inward address and its final convergence of three souls are preserved.

title: So Dense, That Hardly Moving…
text:
So dense, that hardly moving
already within you, you sustain my journey
loaded with weight.

You support not only sloping earth,
but ages: millennia, like your own,
we float in you… Softly and tenderly
you carry me through
endless noons of sun.

To lighten this burden of myself
I surrender to your fabulous density
complete immobility. And I walk.
I walk across your crackling canvases of algae,
through your liquid sapphire, your spilled emerald,
as through the pure blue marble of the sky.

High, quiet gallery of your firmament,
coming wholly near to me!
My eyes opening, certain,
inside you; seers of you, yours,
and fulfilled eyes of immortal waiting!
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The sea’s paradoxical density, its colors, and the speaker’s movement within apparent stillness are retained.

title: I Do Not Ask You Where You Take Me
text:
I do not ask you where you take me.

Nor why.

Nor what for.

You want to walk? Then I follow you.

I carry stars, stars, in my right hand. And I carry stars,
stars, in my left hand.

Tell me, man of all moonlit nights, which hand will
kiss me?

Why have you taken your hands away from me, hands that
caressed my forehead so often and so well?

For you to love me again, I would give you a necklace of
islands, a nervous system of horizons.
I would open, for you, every morning upon your lips!

I am stronger than you, because I lean on you.

Lean out over me, for I am a tower!
Lean out over me: I am that palm tree in your orchard,
that beat with you!
Cast my bells and my palms into the air!
I am your panorama.
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The direct address, repeated stars and hands, and final transformation into tower, palm, and panorama are preserved.

title: Abandoning Ourselves to You
text:
Soft and unsinkable liquid platform
on which we walk, weightless,
advancing trustingly within you…
Was the sea’s salt as dense in Tiberias
as yours?

Strangers to all that is not you, we go
across your level plain, the underwater
estate of the Mar Menor, and Palestine
blazes with palms and almond trees,
in prickly bonfires of prickly pears.

Goats of gray, ash-colored fleece
bleat with their young under the murmuring shelter
of primeval groves… Wine sleeps
in earthen skins, and groaning waterwheels
rescue fresh water from its confinement.

Ah, my burning eyes, my voice of fire
against tender flints at your touch, my sea!
To remain still is to go among your hands
that awaken from sleep.
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The Mar Menor is fused with Tiberias and Palestine through water, salt, palms, and biblical imagery.

title: This That Ends Is Me. I Cannot Pass Beyond Myself…
text:
This that ends is me. I cannot pass beyond myself.
I have reached my own edges;
I would overflow, spilling myself, if I wished
to knock at the Gate of God.

A gaze in itself; all the senses
inside themselves… I am now
the creature’s total limit.

I am going to affirm myself before No, to cry that I came
swollen with an inexpressible heartbeat;
and that I hope hands will sustain me
without the earth’s flesh.

Everything arrived with me;
I brought fabulous miseries, absorbed,
and a very thin branchwork of joys
that dreamed of being a forest of love in the world.

From here I do not expect to spring.
No one calls me.
Am I to persist like a shadow
before your voice, never heard?
Attend to me, mystery; I cannot reach you.
Are you stillness, are you violence
of stillness…?
Are you myself?
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The speaker’s edge, overflow, confrontation with No, and final self-question remain deliberately unresolved.

title: Before You
text:
Because being the same, you are different
and distant from all who look
at that rose of light you pour always
from your sky to your sea, the field I love.

My field, of love never confessed;
of a guarded, modest love,
like an ancient virgin enduring
in my body beside your eternal one.

I have come to love you, to have you tell me
your words of sea and palms;
your mills of salty canvas
that refresh the thirst of so much time.

I abandon myself in your sea, leave myself yours
as one must give oneself to be yours.
If I closed my eyes I would become
a being and a voice: drowned alive.

Have I come, and gone; will I go tomorrow
and come as today…? What other creature
will return for you, to stay
or escape in your light toward the never?
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The beloved landscape’s identity, modest erotic devotion, and final movement toward the unknown are preserved.

title: Sphere Ringed by Spheres That Cannot…
text:
Sphere ringed by spheres that cannot
escape the single sphere.
Spherical hands encircling legs
that embrace one another, round, perfect.
If this sphere that I am now, that I have always been,
were to tear a ring from itself and throw it,
it would fall,
caught by its end, extending
until it trod the dust.

It would ripple for centuries, and its music
would rise through tremors to the sphere
that holds it forever, so entirely its own.
It would be vertical, until a century
made the curve claim to be round
from a dawn without rhythm. It would rise
once more to become a ring, drowning itself
for love of an unfading longing
in the total sphere.

I have been a ring,
trembling as I fell, and upright
I let myself run from the ages…
But the sphere felt that at last my essence
must rest in what is round.
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The poem’s circular geometry, temporal stretching, and return of the ring into the whole are kept literal.

title: Field and Sea, So Joined in a Canticle…
text:
Field and sea, so joined in one canticle,
man has found only rarely in the world.
Sailor and farmer, together;
with earth and net, a single trade.

The sowed fields of sea and land
offer themselves to one family.
The blue meadows of the waters,
and the soft earth the sun drinks in.

A single gaze takes in the whole:
the miracle of bread and fish.
The shepherd walks upon the waters,
and the tree of his cross grows close by.

Palms in flocks, carob trees,
olives and almond groves, pomegranates
shelter the one who eats from the waters,
mixing sea salt with dark oil.

Oh land of this sea, red and deep,
flowering with mills and saltworks!
I transcend the perpetual architecture
of your being and not-doing, your living force!
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The fusion of farming, fishing, landscape, and Christian bread-and-fish imagery is preserved.

title: The Little Working Girl
text:
I am Dominga Villalba;
I was born in the furrow
where my mother sowed.

The hammock that served as my cradle
was braided by absence
and hung by oblivion.
Pablo, they say, was his name.
He never came to see me!

The road of the poor
is found always
only by pain.

Papers, sealed with injustice.
Rifles, loaded with ignominy.

Shack, fields, hopes, everything!
was someone else’s.
Ours,
only a little
of calloused flesh
and a great love fed
by earth, dew,
birds and ears of grain.

Now I am Dominga Villalba,
a worker,
rebellious and combative,
voice and fist in the struggle
for bread and land.
That is how they made me!
With blows they worked
my country clay
and now I am
steel fiber!
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The class struggle and transformation remain intact.

title: To the Brush on the Wall
text:
There is a brush that sings upon the wall,
with new rhythm, old realities.
It brings ancient clarities to the present,
heightens a dark present in shadows.

But it is a brush named for the future,
and whatever it touches in life is changed.
To give shape to an idea it deforms
into great eyes, into immense fists.

It is a brush of old and new make,
the brush of always, the true one,
which in every age finds its timber,
bold and timely at once.

It is a brave brush, a pure brush
that stoops to no false charity;
it paints truths, works for truth,
steady its pulse, its heart secure.

It is a sincere brush and I try
to say what its fiber longs for and feels:
to always have that hand and that brow
that carry it singing across the wall.
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The sonnet-like quatrains and the brush’s political and ethical force are preserved.

title: Asunción
text:
My city is of sand and heavy wind,
with pieces of moon at the corners,
medallions of shadow in the gardens
and an air of terror over the roofs.

No one will come, however much you shout.
No one will answer, however much you call.
It has raised walls of silence
that drown words in the air.

My city is of endless streets
and you will not leave it however far you walk.
The fearsome Taú-taú¹ of will-o’-the-wisp fire
will make you lose your way if you depart;
it will turn you into a restless ghost,
make you wander through courtyards and entryways,
entangle you in the strings of Indian harps
and in the sweet language of honeycombs.

My city will wrap you in its lace
like a spider’s thread and foam²
and you will want to react, and it will be too late.
You will be one more prisoner among its prisoners
or the gray shadow dissolving
in the deep river that embraces it.

But since it is of sand and heavy wind
it will have flown away whole in the morning.

END

¹ Taú-taú: a firebird that deceives men in the forest, making them follow false paths.
² Ñandutí: lace whose name means what it resembles: a spider’s nest.
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. Explanatory notes are translated as supplied; the city’s folkloric menace and final vanishing are retained.

title: The Wounded Lark
text:
I cannot sing to you, son of my land.
My voice, entwined with your crown of thorns,
can only bleed for your wounds.

I cannot sing of your misery,
of your hookworm weakness,
of the emptiness of your accustomed hunger.
I cannot sing of your chains,
of the yoke that bends your back,
of the bare cot beneath the roof that rains
its straw importance.

I cannot sing to you and I do not sing.
Let the blind lark sing for you,
in its artistic walled-in cage,
its stupidity of perfumed flowers,
loves, kisses, crystalline waters.
Let the murmuring stream speak to you,
of the singing spring that descends,
of jasmine perfuming our streets
on moonlit nights.
Let the blind lark sing to you; I see
your hospital fate without bandages:
I am the wounded lark.

I cannot sing to you and I do not sing.
I cry out in your voice of rebellion,
I strike in your liberating fist.
I am brick in your walled chest,
a flash in your drilling gaze,
a word in your message of solidarity.
I am fiber of your flesh at work,
flame in the torch that raises
the triumphal arch of your arm.—
I yearn with your deferred desires:
today I cannot sing to you; tomorrow I will,
when your voice can sing with mine
the joy of the liberated homeland!
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The speaker’s refusal of ornamental consolation and final solidarity with the worker’s liberation are preserved.

title: Still, Because I Always Watch You, Even Sleeping…
text:
Still, because I always watch you, even sleeping,
I see others reach you,
taking off their distinguishing clothes,
and entering your sustaining flesh…

If I did not await the miracle, I would weep!
But the miracle is always there, because you burnish and polish them
like pieces of stone, and radiant
they display their own fire from your light.

Beautiful, they are beautiful, those you take into yourself.
Creatures dazzled by your touch.
Men and women newly made,
perfect in flesh and soul, sparkling
upon your own sparkle.

Joy that the wretched in beauty,
the slow of earth, the clumsy and the healthy come here!
Joy for my eyes, your two fires,
which are saved by your miracle,
oh merciful sea of mine!
that turns lead and clay to gold!
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The sea’s refining, almost sacramental transformation is preserved.

title: Naked You Demand Them, to Dress Them in You…
text:
Naked you demand the creatures, to dress them in you,
to cast these transparent, pure cloaks over their shoulders,
transforming flesh into soul;
snatching away the age-old dust of the soil,
washing them of furrow, fermented pollen,
the fruit-acid of harvests.

They are your jewels when you bathe them.
Purified of their seven black bulls, if you touch them.
Sparkling with almost human virtues
through your divine contact.

You corrode their bark,
dissolve their ripe, scaly tunics.
You save, like John’s baptism,
a whole genesis of sins.

Yes. Naked, your hoarse and delicate shell awaits us
to be born again in the sea that you are
into a peace of the spirit, set free.

Like microscopic lava we leave on your shore
the dirty sands of sorrowful sins.
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The poem’s baptismal cleansing and geological imagery are retained.

title: We Are All Silent, Listening for You to Speak…
text:
We are all silent, listening for you to speak,
and though we do not understand everything, you enumerate for us
your ancient mysteries, pure bone of life
that the sun consumes incessantly beside your voice.

It is the father’s story and the son’s living story
that your wave carries, ardent, dense word
covering us with foam of frantic saltiness;
or with calm, floating like the color of light.

You smell and taste of mollusk, bitter wave; you cross us,
a sweet shove invading like love…
you make us dizzy like a height, cleave us
like a moon-sword…!

We all close our eyes. Who comes walking,
hardly touching the waves…?
Who multiplies the catch and snatches crowds away?
Are you a sea, or that lake the sun of wrath dried?
Are you the sea, or a mirror descended from heaven
so that we, yours, might dream the sea?

Moon of you, vibrant and swift-stepping moon,
in these waiting nights the boats drip away
on a road beyond the world, my sea!
September moon, last,
no longer fearless or strange,
in this broken mystery of your distance…!

Tell us of the sea; if you can, moon, tell us
how they made this sea:
if at the same time as you, if before;
if when you opened your chalice it was already here,
watching us…
If afterward you heard
the rumor of its bursting… Tell us.

We are still, listening
beneath light; silent
and trembling with light!
So close are we to the sea and to you,
silent moon!
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The sea, moon, and creation questions remain suspended in their liturgical cadence.

title: The Water of the Sky Mingling with the Water of the Sea…
text:
The water of the sky mingling with the water of the sea.
Swimming through them in the boat advancing in silence,
with ecstatic estrangement, frantic insistence
that it never end, that it always remain there,
with me, clasping me in vertiginous rite,
the two twin waters, the two identical waters,
the two eternal pure waters in which the moon
magically disintegrated.

And today, radiant, unique day of September,
joy of the two blue seas, one and two in the same,
shores of La Manga, burning with earth!
which hold and separate them, divide and join them
in the endless double Junction, the key
to this sea, so intimate and complex.

Today, yes, my two seas in their double contact,
in alternating, unison surrender of force,
the two seas loved as one, the one they are,
the immense sea that is sky for every water,
with sun and moon, wind and catch;
with this volcanic rhythm of buried ardor
in sweet, almost mystical geology.

Night and morning of the sea, round dense day
of sun and phantoms slipping through blue light
of a long voyage in a boat that falls silent
so I can hear, mine, hard and compact,
the terrible pulse, delicately full,
of a sun-sea, a moon-sea;
of dreaming or remembering oneself in sleep,
of living or burning in the light…

You, always you, stranger and ours at every hour,
clean and fragrant, scented and light, strong and populated,
an entire universe inside the lantern without escape
that is this land’s voracious embrace!
editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. ‘La Manga’ and the poem’s sea/sky doubling are retained.
